paper.title: MNL-Bandit: A Dynamic Learning Approach to Assortment Selection

settings.name_in_paper: MNL-Bandit with totally unimodular (downward-closed) assortment constraints, v_i <= v_0
unmapped: Multinomial logit (MNL) choice model: offering assortment S, the customer purchases product i in S with probability v_i/(v_0+sum_{j in S} v_j) or nothing; the learner observes which product (if any) was purchased
Expected revenue R(S,v) = sum_{i in S} r_i v_i/(1+sum_{j in S} v_j) is nonlinear in the parameters
No-purchase most likely: v_i <= v_0 = 1 for all products (Assumption 4.1)
Feasible assortments given by totally unimodular constraints A x(S) <= b and downward closed
The learner knows the product revenues r_i in [0,1] and the number of products N
settings.definition_quote: at every time instance $t$, the seller selects  an assortment $S_t \subset \{1, \ldots, N\}$ and observes the customer purchase decision $c_t \in S_t \cup \{0\}$ ... $Reg_{\pi}(T,\mb{v}) = \sum_{t=1}^T R(S^*,\mb{v}) - \mathbb{E}_{\pi}[R(S_t, \mathbf{v})]$

Exploration-Exploitation algorithm for MNL-Bandit general parameters (Algorithm 3)

conditions: feasible family downward closed (Assumption 4.1), totally unimodular constraints

source.label: main_result
source.quote: For any instance $\mb{v} = (v_0, \ldots, v_N)$ of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products,  $r_i\in [0,1]$ and Assumption \ref{assumption1}, the regret of the policy given by Algorithm~\ref{learn_algo} at any time $T$ is bounded as, $Reg_\pi(T,\mb{v}) \leq C_1\sqrt{NT\log{{N}T}} + C_2N\log^2{{N}T}$, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are absolute constants

results.notes: C_1, C_2 absolute constants, so recorded as O. Regret defined via expected revenues (pseudo-regret).

symbols.Delta_v: difference between expected revenues of the optimal and second-best assortment

source.label: assymptotic_bound
source.quote: For any instance $\mb{v} = (v_0, \ldots, v_N)$ of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products,  $r_i\in [0,1]$ and Assumption \ref{assumption1}, the regret of the policy given by Algorithm~\ref{learn_algo} at any time $T$ is bounded as, $Reg_\pi(T,\mb{v}) \leq B_1\left(\frac{N^2\log{T}}{\Delta(\mb{v})}\right) + B_2$, where $B_1$ and $B_2$ are absolute constants.

results.notes: Additive constant B_2 absorbed into O. The proof actually yields log(NT) terms; recorded as stated.

symbols.Delta_v: difference between expected revenues of the optimal and second-best assortment

source.label: parameter_bound_cardinality
source.quote: For any instance $\mb{v} = (v_0, \ldots, v_N)$ of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products and cardinality constraint $K$,  $r_i\in [0,1]$ and $v_0 \geq v_i$ for all $i,$ the regret of the policy given by Algorithm~\ref{learn_algo} at any time $T$ is bounded as, $Reg_\pi(T,\mb{v}) \leq B_1\frac{NK\log{{N}T}}{\Delta(\mb{v})} + B_2$

results.notes: Paper's K (cardinality) is m. Algorithm does not need Delta.

conditions: feasible family downward closed, totally unimodular constraints

source.label: main_result_extn
source.quote: For any instance $\mb{v} = (v_0, \ldots, v_N)$, of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products,  $r_i\in [0,1]$ for all $i=1,\ldots, N$,  the regret of the policy corresponding to Algorithm~\ref{learn_algo_extn} at any time $T$ is bounded as, $Reg_{\pi}(T,\mb{v}) \leq  C_1\sqrt{BNT\log{{N}T}} + C_2N\log^2{{N}T}+C_3 N B \log{{N}T}$, where $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ are absolute constants and $B = \max\{\max_{i} \frac{v_i}{v_0},1\}$.

source.label: unconstrained_bound
source.quote: For any instance, $\mb{v} = (v_0, \ldots, v_N)$ of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products and no constraints,  $r_i\in [0,1]$ and $v_0\ge v_i$ for $i=1,\ldots, N$, there exists finite constants $C_1$ and $C_2,$ such that the regret ... is bounded as, $Reg_\pi(T,\mb{v}) \leq C_1\sqrt{|S^*|T\log{NT}} + C_2N\log{NT}$.

results.notes: Special case of s1 with no constraints; dependence on |S^*| makes it instance-dependent.

source.label: lower_bound
source.quote: There exists a (randomized) instance of the \banditMNL~problem with $v_0 \geq v_i\;, i=1,\ldots,N$, such that {for any $N$ and $K$},  and any policy $\mathcal{\pi}$ that offers assortment $\mathcal{S}_t^{\mathcal{\pi}}$, $|{S}_t^{\mathcal{\pi}}| \leq K$ at time $t$, we have for all $T\geq N$ that,$$Reg_\pi(T,\mb{v}) ... \geq C\sqrt{\frac{NT}{K}},$$ where ... $C$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Expectation also over the random instance. Paper's K is m. C absolute constant.

symbols.eps_inst: bias of the best arm, epsilon = (1/100) sqrt(K*alpha_b/T)
symbols.alpha_b: Bernoulli mean of non-optimal arms, alpha < 1

conditions: K >= 2 Bernoulli arms, one uniformly random arm with mean alpha+epsilon, others alpha

source.label: lower_bound_MAB
source.quote: For any $N \geq 2$, $\alpha<1$, $T$ and any online algorithm  $\mathcal{A}$ that plays arm $\mathcal{A}_t$ at time $t$, the expected regret on instance $I_{\sf MAB}$ is at least $\displaystyle \frac{\epsilon T}{6}$.

results.notes: Paper's N arms = K. With the stated epsilon, the bound is sqrt(K*alpha*T)/600. The appendix proof uses epsilon = sqrt(N/(60 alpha T)) and N >= 12, an inconsistency; described as an extension of the standard lower bound.
